title: Finite reduction preserves the canonical adjoint mates
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $B=A_{E,m}$ with $1\le m\le n$. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. On their small pro-etale sites use $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories, and $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. Use pullback, compact supports, tensor, and exceptional adjunctions as in [def-pur-co-smoothness, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], their canonical coefficient comparisons [lem-fix-operation-reduction, lem-coef-finite-exceptional], and the projection map of [def-exchange-projection].

For a smooth separated $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, put $\omega_{f,A}=Rf_A^!A_Y$ and let $\theta_{f,A,K}:Lf_A^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}\to Rf_A^!K$ be the canonical tensor map specified in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Under the pullback, tensor and exceptional coefficient comparisons,
$$Q_X(\theta_{f,A,K})=\theta_{f,B,Q_YK}.$$
For composable smooth separated maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ of pure relative dimensions, the canonical exceptional composition comparison $c_{g,f,A}:R(gf)_A^!\xrightarrow\sim Rf_A^!Rg_A^!$ is also identified by reduction with $c_{g,f,B}$. For a Cartesian square with this $f$, arbitrary $v:Y'\to Y$, and projections $u:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, reduction identifies the canonical extraordinary comparison $\beta_{f,v,A,K}:Lu^*Rf_A^!K\to Rf_A'^!Lv^*K$ with $\beta_{f,v,B,Q_YK}$; at $K=A_Y$ these are the coefficient-object comparisons of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Finally, for any separated finite-type $h:T\to U$, $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ and $a:Rh_{!,A}M\to L$, reduction identifies the adjoint transpose $Rh_A^!(a)\circ\eta_{A,M}$ with the transpose of the reduced $a$, under the compact-support and exceptional coefficient comparisons.

proof.text: Finite-type schemes over the standing field are Noetherian (finiteMate_noetherian). Use the existing Nagata compactifications. The coefficient rings are finite at positive levels, and finiteComparedInvertibleExponent supplies their invertible-exponent hypothesis. For base change, the source-library smooth exceptional finite-Tor preservation theorem gives finite Tor amplitude and bounded constructibility of the exceptional image of K. Tensor with the scalar coefficient sheaf and reflect the resulting homological lower bound through exact faithful scalar restriction. This is the already proved scalar_extension_plus_of_finiteTor helper, which supplies the second bounded-below input to compact-support coefficient coherence.

For the tensor clause specialize the proved generic finite-ring helper ExceptionalCoefficients.tensorCompatibility, accessed by a proof-only import all of ExceptionalCoefficientComparison, to the actual lifted coefficient quotient. Its ordered projection counit-transpose calculation uses the stated compact-scalar projection equation, scalar right-unit equation and ordered tensor coefficient mate lemma; it applies to every object and does not specialize coefficient rings to Z/l^r. Thus its conclusion is definitionally finiteAdjointMateTensorClause, including the published tensor-domain and coefficient-unit maps. No origin witness or new geometric comparison is introduced.

Use smooth exceptional finite-Tor preservation for the composite f ≫ g to put its exceptional image of K and its scalar extension in D+. Apply etaleCompactScalarComposition to that image. Its q maps are exactly chosenCompactSupportIso.hom. The proved private finiteMate_composition calculation forms the composite scalar comparison qp, computes the counit of b_f followed by G_f(b_g) using counit naturality and the two mateMap_counit equations, and applies coefficient_exchange_of_counit_at to the compact-support compositors. The conjugateEquiv_counit identities identify their right mates with finiteExceptionalComposition. The resulting equation is exactly the composition clause. No new theorem with sorry and no purity orientation are introduced.

For the given arbitrary Cartesian square use the proved compact_scalar_exchange_left helper, which expresses etaleCompactScalarBaseChange in the specified left-derived pullback coordinates. Evaluate at the exceptional image of K with the lower bounds of Step 1. Invert its four isomorphisms and cancel the two compact-support scalar comparisons, producing the inverse-exchange coefficient cube at that object. The extraordinary maps are definitionally mateEquiv of the inverse compact-support exchange. Apply coefficient_exchange_of_counit_at with their mate counit equations and the proved generic mateMap_counit equations. Its equality, reversed, is finiteAdjointMateBaseChangeClause for this supplied square. No passage to a chosen pullback object, no flatness of the base map and no exceptional comparison invertibility are used.

For the intrinsic finite-Tor transpose clause expand the functor image of the unit followed by G(a). Naturality of the specified transformation b moves Q(G(a)) across b. Since b is defined to be mateEquiv of inverse q, unit_mateEquiv replaces Q(unit) followed by b with the reduced unit followed by G(q inverse). Functoriality combines G(q inverse) and G(Q(a)). This proves the displayed equality directly without the bundled finite_exceptional theorem.
